description: We are a multi-disciplinary team focused on tackling deep research-intensive space challenges. Combining backgrounds in coding, hardware development, and data analysis, we aim to bridge fundamental science with practical software solutions. Our technical interests span Earth science, astrophysics, and space exploration. We are looking for team members with strong research skills, analytical minds, or deep knowledge in physics, chemistry, and biology to help us synthesize academic data.
summary:
LUNA-TERRA is a planetary-analogue evidence explorer developed for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge. It brings together three distinct evidence streams: (1) geospatial inspection of a published lunar south-polar research dataset around the PNS02 exploration area; (2) independent analysis of NASA LOLA Site07 elevation and slope rasters at 5 m/pixel; and (3) a literature-based evidence matrix for five terrestrial research candidates: the Atacama Desert, Haughton Crater, McMurdo Dry Valleys, Lonar Crater, and Río Tinto.

The PNS02 module loads 141 PSR features and identifies five positive-area polygon intersections while exposing source attributes and unresolved discrepancies. The NASA module calculates descriptive statistics for the complete Site07 raster tile; it is not spatially registered to PNS02. The Earth-analogue matrix summarizes published research, specific purposes, and limitations; candidates have not been quantitatively assessed or ranked by LUNA-TERRA.

By keeping evidence streams separate and making uncertainty visible, the platform supports transparent, purpose-specific analogue research without claiming complete planetary replicas or landing-site suitability.
details:
DETAILED PROJECT DESCRIPTION

Project Overview

LUNA-TERRA is an individually developed research and geospatial evidence platform created for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge. Its objective is to investigate how selected terrestrial environments can help researchers understand specific geological, environmental and operational processes relevant to lunar and Martian exploration.

Rather than assuming that visual resemblance establishes an analogy, LUNA-TERRA organizes scientific evidence, source datasets, derived measurements and limitations into an accessible interactive platform.

1. PNS02 Geospatial Evidence Explorer

The current lunar case study uses the complementary research dataset associated with Wueller et al. (2026), available through Zenodo under CC BY 4.0.

The application loads 141 permanently shadowed region (PSR) source features and a uniquely identified PNS02 exploration-area polygon. It performs projected-coordinate geometry operations, identifies five positive-area polygon intersections, and allows visitors to inspect individual source records.

The interface includes two map modes, a feature selector, an attribute inspector and a PNS02 reference marker.

The five intersections are geometric findings, not five confirmed landing sites. The project explicitly preserves unresolved discrepancies involving the ID 335 coordinate correspondence, meanAge attributes and volatile aggregation.

2. Independent NASA LOLA Site07 Terrain Evidence

LUNA-TERRA uses the NASA Planetary Geospatial Data Archive Product 78, specifically the Site07 surface-elevation and slope GeoTIFF products.

An offline processing workflow calculates descriptive statistics and generates visualizations from the 5 m/pixel rasters. The application presents elevation and slope distributions, summary statistics and processing provenance.

These statistics describe the complete NASA Site07 raster tile. The NASA product has not been spatially registered to the PNS02 exploration polygon because compatible lunar reference-frame transformations have not been established. The two evidence sources are intentionally kept separate.

3. Earth Analog Evidence Matrix

The application presents five literature-supported terrestrial research candidates:

  • Atacama Desert, Chile — hyperaridity, soil geochemistry and habitability research.
  • Haughton Impact Crater, Canada — impact geology, polar-desert exploration, ground ice and operations.
  • McMurdo Dry Valleys, Antarctica — permafrost, subsurface ice and cold-desert geomorphology.
  • Lonar Crater, India — basaltic impact processes and alteration.
  • Río Tinto, Spain — acidic iron/sulfur geochemistry and astrobiology.

The evidence matrix organizes these candidates through seven comparison dimensions: geology, mineralogy, water and ice, thermal and environmental conditions, terrain, operations, and astrobiology.

These are literature-supported research candidates, not quantitatively assessed or ranked by LUNA-TERRA. Lake Bonney is treated separately as a supporting sub-ice research context.

Technology and Methodology

The application is developed primarily with Python and Streamlit. Geospatial analysis uses Shapely, PyProj and PyShp; numerical and raster processing uses NumPy and Rasterio in the offline data-preparation workflow. The application uses packaged, documented outputs for public deployment.

Source provenance, coordinate-reference limitations, data-quality discrepancies and methodological uncertainty are documented throughout the application and repository.

Current Limitations and Future Research

The current project does not produce a composite planetary-analogue score, rank landing sites, assess landing safety or claim complete Earth–Moon–Mars equivalence.

Future work includes establishing authoritative lunar reference-frame transformations, resolving the remaining PNS02 source-record discrepancies, incorporating suitable uncertainty products, and obtaining matched datasets for quantitative Earth-environment comparisons.

Public application: https://lunaterra-explorer.streamlit.app/

Source repository: https://github.com/AsifurInNctrl/LUNA-TERRA
